title: Tenses Quiz 6
description: Read the time words and pick the tense that fits.
instructions: Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: 'She ___ in Lagos since 2018.'
questions.explanation: Since + a starting point with an unfinished state needs the present perfect. Watch out: lives and is living do not fit since.

questions.question: 'I ___ a great film last night.'
questions.explanation: Last night is a finished time, so the past simple is used. Watch out: finished times never go with the present perfect.

questions.question: 'Right now, the students ___ an exam.'
questions.explanation: Right now points to the present continuous. Watch out: take, in the present simple, would describe a habit.

questions.question: 'My father ___ the newspaper every morning.'
questions.explanation: Every morning shows a habit, so the present simple is used. Watch out: -s is needed with he, she, it.

questions.question: 'By the time we arrived, they ___.'
questions.explanation: By the time + a past action needs the past perfect for the earlier action. Watch out: have left belongs to the present.

questions.question: 'I ___ you tomorrow if I have time.'
questions.explanation: A real condition about tomorrow uses will in the main clause. Watch out: the if clause stays in the present.

questions.question: I {{1}} (live) here for ten years.
questions.explanation: For + a length of time, up to now, needs the present perfect. Watch out: lived would mean you no longer live here.

questions.question: Yesterday at six o'clock, I {{1}} (watch) television.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a past moment uses the past continuous.

questions.question: The word 'ago' goes with the past simple.
questions.explanation: I saw him two days ago. Watch out: 'I have seen him two days ago' is wrong, because ago gives a finished time.

questions.question: Match each time expression with its tense.
questions.explanation: Time words are clues to the tense. Watch out: by + a future time points to the future perfect.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: I am living here since 2019.
accepted: I have been living here since 2019.
I have been living here since 2019
questions.explanation: Since + a starting point needs the present perfect. Watch out: the present continuous cannot be used with since.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I am knowing her since childhood.
I have known her since childhood.
questions.explanation: A state that continues up to now uses the present perfect, and know is a state verb. Watch out: do not use the continuous with know.
